label: LobeChat (lobehub/lobehub, formerly lobe-chat)
version: lobehub/lobehub release v2.3.3 = commit 69f8dcdfae1c59a5ffb703b3a0187223987bcd56 (default branch is 'canary', pushed 2026-11-14; lobehub/lobe-chat redirects to lobehub/lobehub). HTTP layer: openai-node ^6.49.0 (v6.49.0 source read for headers).

sources.note: OpenAI-protocol runtime (also used for custom providers with SDK type 'openai'): default baseURL https://api.openai.com/v1; handlePayload default branch = {...rest, model, stream: payload.stream ?? true}; Responses API is chosen for certain model ids or when enabledSearch is set; reasoning-style model ids go through pruneReasoningPayload; models() = client.models.list() -> processMultiProviderModelList.

Constructor: new OpenAICompatibleClient({apiKey, baseURL, ...}) (extends openai-node OpenAI); baseURL used verbatim, the SDK appends '/chat/completions' and '/models'. Missing apiKey throws invalidAPIKey.

Chat Completions request assembly: apiMode/preserveThinking stripped, messages converted, 'user' = options.user, prompt_cache_key only for gpt-*/o<digit> model ids, stream_options {include_usage:true} whenever stream is true, openai SDK call with headers {Accept: '*/*'}.

Message conversion: content string kept, parts arrays filtered; name / tool_calls / tool_call_id / function_call / reasoning_content preserved when present; tool messages with images are flattened to text + a following user message.
filterOutgoingContentParts: an assistant turn whose content parts all vanish becomes content null when it has tool_calls, else ''.

pruneReasoningPayload (only for OpenAI reasoning-style model ids): system->developer, frequency/presence_penalty forced 0, stream_options/logprobs removed, temperature/top_p dropped unless reasoning effort is none.

Stream consumer: tolerates chunks with empty/missing choices (usage-only chunks), reads choices[0].delta (content, reasoning_content, tool_calls), finish_reason, usage; does not require delta.role or [DONE].
Non-stream completions are replayed as synthetic stream chunks: reads choices[].message.content/role/tool_calls/finish_reason, data.usage, id, created, model.

Model list for custom (sdk 'openai') providers: GET /models, list.data.filter() dropping ids that CONTAIN any of embedding, davinci, curie, moderation, ada, babbage, tts, whisper, dall-e (case-insensitive); reads item.id (string) and optional item.created (number seconds/ms, or date string).
processMultiProviderModelList (built-in OpenAI provider list): input type Array<{id: string}>; abilities (function calling, vision, reasoning ...) are guessed from keywords in the model id.
DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG.params = {frequency_penalty: 0, presence_penalty: 0, temperature: 1, top_p: 1}; enableStreaming defaults true (L25-L40).

Browser-side getChatCompletion: merges {model, stream, ...DEFAULT params} with agent params + apiMode ('responses' if the provider's Responses API switch is on, else 'chatCompletion'); nulls removed; posts to /webapi/chat/<provider> (server mode) or, with 'Use Client Request Mode', runs the model runtime in the browser (fetchOnClient).
fetchOnClient: requires a signed-in user, then initializeWithClientStore -> ModelRuntime with dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true (clientModelRuntime.ts L32-L45) -> openai-node running in the browser.
Server route: modelRuntime.chat(data, {user: userId, ...}) so the upstream request carries user = the LobeChat user id; awaitFirstResponseChunk() turns an empty completion into a structured error.

Provider 'Connectivity Check' button: chatService.fetchPresetTaskResult with messages [{content:'hello', role:'user'}] and the selected check model, normal streaming path; passes only if some text comes back.

Structured output (non-stream): response_format {json_schema, type:'json_schema'} + user; if the upstream error text matches /(response_format|json_schema)...(unavailable|not support)/ it retries once with a forced tool call (tools [{function:{description,name,parameters},type:'function'}], tool_choice {function:{name},type:'function'}).
Topic-title prompt and TOPIC_TITLE_JSON_SCHEMA {name:'topic_title', strict:true, schema:{type:'object', properties:{title:{type:'string'}}, required:['title'], additionalProperties:false}}.

System-agent defaults used for utility tasks (topic auto-summary etc.): DEFAULT_MODEL deepseek-v4-flash/provider deepseek, DEFAULT_MINI_MODEL gpt-5.6-luna/provider openai - i.e. utility calls do NOT automatically use the user's chat model unless the 'System Agent' settings are pointed at the gateway.

Default request headers of openai-node: Accept application/json, User-Agent, X-Stainless-Retry-Count, (X-Stainless-Timeout when a per-request timeout is set), platform headers, OpenAI-Organization/OpenAI-Project when set, Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>.
Platform headers: X-Stainless-Lang js, -Package-Version, -OS, -Arch, -Runtime (node | browser:<name>), -Runtime-Version (browser: OS 'Unknown', Arch 'unknown').

Tool history conversion: assistant gets tool_calls [{function:{arguments,name}, id, type:'function'}]; tool messages get name = generated tool name + original tool_call_id. Tools are only used when the model has function-calling ability (isCanUseFC).
UI labels: 'API Proxy URL' (placeholder https://your-proxy-url.com/v1), 'Connectivity Check' / 'Check', 'Use Client Request Mode' ('will initiate session requests directly from the browser').

setup.baseUrl: http://<gateway-host>:8787/v1  (WITH /v1: LobeChat passes the value as the openai-node baseURL, the SDK appends '/chat/completions' and '/models'). Settings > AI Service Provider > OpenAI (or '+ Add Custom Provider' with request format 'OpenAI') > field 'API Proxy URL' (custom provider: 'Proxy URL').
setup.model: Models are added in the provider's model list: either 'Fetch models' (calls GET /v1/models) or add a custom model id by hand, e.g. agent/sample, then select it in the chat header. For the 'Check' button choose that model in the dropdown next to it.
setup.apiKey: 'API Key' field of the provider (required: LobeChat refuses to build the client without a non-empty key).
setup.notes: Two modes. DEFAULT = server-side request: browser -> LobeChat server /webapi/chat/<provider> -> gateway, request made by openai-node in Node (headers Accept: */*, User-Agent: OpenAI/JS <ver>, X-Stainless-* = js/<ver>/<os>/<arch>/node/<node-version>, Authorization), body also carries user = LobeChat user id. In Docker use host.docker.internal for the gateway. 'Use Client Request Mode' (per-provider switch, requires being signed in) = the browser runs openai-node itself and calls the gateway DIRECTLY: needs CORS and sends X-Stainless-* browser headers (X-Stainless-Runtime: browser:<name>), no 'user' field. Hazards: (a) the per-provider 'Responses API' switch (and enabledSearch for OpenAI-type providers) makes LobeChat call POST /v1/responses instead of chat/completions - keep it off; (b) model abilities (function calling, vision, reasoning) are guessed from keywords in the model id or set manually, so for a plain agent id LobeChat will usually NOT send tools or images unless the user ticks those abilities; (c) the model list for custom providers hides ids that contain 'embedding','davinci','curie','moderation','ada','babbage','tts','whisper','dall-e' as a substring (e.g. 'agent/adapter' or 'agent/canada'); (d) topic title / summary / translation helpers run on separately configured 'System Agent' models (defaults deepseek-v4-flash@deepseek and gpt-5.6-luna@openai) so they never reach the gateway unless the user points them at it; (e) chat requests are re-sent through the agent runtime which may add extra system context messages, so exact message lists below are representative, not exhaustive.

cases.title: Provider 'Fetch models': GET /v1/models via openai-node (server side)

evidence.note: client.models.list() (openai-node GET <baseURL>/models, no query). Headers are the SDK defaults (L1164-L1181 of openai-node client.ts); X-Stainless-OS/Arch/Runtime-Version values are examples of the Node host. Whether the model-list call is made server-side or in the browser under Client Request Mode was not verified.

cases.notes: list.data must be an array (the code does list.data.filter / modelsPage.data.map - a missing 'data' throws); each item's id must be a string (item.id.toLowerCase()). 'created' is optional and may be a number (seconds or 13-digit ms) or a date string. 'object' and 'owned_by' are never read. An empty list is accepted (no models appear). On any non-2xx the UI shows 'Failed to fetch models: <message>' and the user can still add models by hand. Ids containing embedding/davinci/curie/moderation/ada/babbage/tts/whisper/dall-e are dropped for custom providers.

cases.title: Provider 'Check' button: streaming 'hello' with default params (server side, user field present)

evidence.note: Browser payload = merge({model, stream:true, ...DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG.params}, {messages:[{content:'hello',role:'user'}], model, apiMode:'chatCompletion'}) (services/chat/index.ts L349-L363); server adds user (route.ts L47-L49), runtime strips apiMode and adds stream_options (chat.ts L136-L147). Key order in JSON follows the object spreads and is not significant.

cases.notes: Check passes only if non-empty text arrives; an empty completion or a stream with zero chunks becomes an error (awaitFirstResponseChunk). The stream parser tolerates a final usage-only chunk with choices: [], does not require delta.role on the first chunk, does not require [DONE] (openai-node ends at EOF or [DONE]) and ignores unknown fields; a chunk with a top-level 'error' object makes openai-node throw. An agent whose id looks like an OpenAI reasoning model (o1/o3/gpt-5...) takes a different path: pruneReasoningPayload then drops stream_options, temperature and top_p, forces penalties to 0 and rewrites role 'system' to 'developer' (this case is not replayed here because it depends on the id pattern, see openai/modelId.ts).

cases.title: Normal streaming chat message (default agent params, server side)

evidence.note: Parameter keys/values verified (same as the connectivity check). The exact messages list is built by the context-engine pipeline (system role from the agent, history, optional injected context blocks) and was not fully traced; plain text user/assistant turns are plain strings (MessageContent.ts L268, L524), system content is a string.

cases.notes: temperature 1 and top_p 1 are sent TOGETHER (no Claude-style conflict handling for non-Claude model ids). 'name' is passed through if a message has one (multi-agent group chats). No max_tokens by default.

cases.title: Streaming chat with agent sampling settings maxed out (temperature, top_p, penalties, max_tokens)

evidence.note: ChatStreamPayload declares max_tokens, temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, n, logprobs, top_logprobs, response_format, tool_choice, ...; getChatCompletion merges the agent's saved params over the defaults. That the agent settings UI actually fills max_tokens (and with this key name) was not traced to the UI; the rest is verified.

cases.notes: LobeChat does not expose n/seed/stop/logit_bias in the normal chat UI.

cases.title: Streaming disabled in the agent's chat settings: stream:false, no stream_options

evidence.note: includeUsageRequested = Boolean(stream && ...), so stream_options is undefined (dropped) when stream is false; the stream flag comes from chatConfig.enableStreaming !== false (services/chat/index.ts L352). Response is replayed as a synthetic stream (nonStreamToStream.ts).

cases.notes: Opt-in (chat setting 'streaming' off). id/created/model are copied into the synthetic chunks; message.role is copied into delta.role; tool_calls and reasoning_content are optional extras; usage is optional (only used if present). Not enabled by default.

cases.title: Agent with plugins/skills on a function-calling-capable model: tools array, no tool_choice

evidence.note: Tools are produced by the ToolsEngine and passed as params.tools (services/chat/index.ts L271); gated by the model's functionCall ability. The tool object shape {type:'function', function:{description,name,parameters}} follows ChatCompletionTool; tool_choice / parallel_tool_calls are never set by the normal chat path (ChatStreamPayload.tool_choice exists but no default) - absence not exhaustively verified. Tool names/parameters below are illustrative; real LobeChat tool names are generated as '<identifier><separator><apiName>'.

messages.content: What is the weather in Paris?

function.description: Get the current weather for a city
function.name: weather____getWeather

cases.notes: The tool-name separator in the example is a guess ('____'); function names are otherwise opaque strings. Streamed tool_calls deltas (index, id, function.name/arguments) are consumed; an assistant tool call whose function is null throws 'Invalid tool call: function is null'.

cases.title: Next turn after a tool call: assistant with tool_calls and empty content, then role:tool message with name

evidence.note: convertOpenAIMessages output shape verified (content, role, name, tool_calls, tool_call_id); assistant content is '' (string passes through) or null (when all content parts vanish and tool_calls exist, contextBuilders/openai.ts L114-L123). tool message 'name' comes from ToolCall.ts L181-L196. Tool name format in the example is illustrative.

messages.content: What is the weather in Paris?

function.description: Get the current weather for a city
function.name: weather____getWeather

cases.notes: Gateway should accept assistant content '' or null alongside tool_calls, and role:tool messages carrying a 'name' key. For model ids containing deepseek/glm/kimi LobeChat may also echo 'reasoning_content' on assistant tool-call turns.

cases.title: Model setting 'reasoning effort' enabled: reasoning_effort key added (non-reasoning model id)

evidence.note: params spreads modelParams.resolvedExtendParams (decided by @lobechat/mecha from the model card's extendParams and the agent's chatConfig); ChatStreamPayload.reasoning_effort is typed (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max). That a custom model's extendParams 'reasoningEffort' maps to the key 'reasoning_effort' (and not to 'reasoning'/'effort'/'thinking' variants, which also exist in the type) was not verified. Off by default for ids without that extend param.

cases.notes: Other extend-param keys LobeChat can add for some model families (not for plain ids): enabledContextCaching, thinking {type,budget_tokens}, thinkingBudget, thinkingLevel, effort, text.verbosity, imageAspectRatio, ... Unknown top-level keys are forwarded verbatim by the OpenAI runtime.

cases.title: Structured output (topic title / helpers): non-stream, response_format json_schema strict + user

evidence.note: Request shape verified from generateObjectViaJsonSchema (messages, model, response_format {json_schema, type:'json_schema'}, user; reasoning_effort only when given); headers are the SDK defaults (no Accept override: options.headers is undefined). That the topic-title feature uses this call, with TOPIC_TITLE_JSON_SCHEMA (summaryTitle.ts L5-L16), and which model it runs on (the 'System Agent' setting, default deepseek-v4-flash@deepseek) was not traced end to end.

messages.content:
You are a professional conversation summarizer. Generate a concise title that captures the essence of the conversation.

Rules:
- Return one JSON object with a single "title" string matching the supplied schema
- No explanations or additional fields
- Maximum 15 words
- Maximum 80 characters
- No punctuation marks
- Use the language specified by the locale code: zh-CN
- The title should accurately reflect the main topic of the conversation
- Keep it short and to the point

<task>
Generate a concise title that captures the essence of the conversation.
</task>

<conversation>
<user>
Hello
</user>
<assistant>
Hi, how can I help?
</assistant>
</conversation>

cases.notes: Response: choices[0].message.content must be a JSON string matching the schema (parseStructuredOutputText); usage optional. No stream key and no stream_options in this request. If the gateway answers a 400/422 whose message matches /(response_format|json_schema).*(unavailable|not +support)/i, LobeChat retries once with tools [{function:{description,name:'topic_title',parameters:<schema>},type:'function'}] and tool_choice {function:{name:'topic_title'},type:'function'} (non-stream) and then reads choices[0].message.tool_calls[*].function.arguments.

cases.title: Vision-capable model with an attached image: user content array [text, image_url]

evidence.note: Array shape verified (text part first, then image_url parts built from imageList / stored image_url parts; detail 'auto' appears in some builders, MessageContent.ts L653); if the model lacks the vision ability images are replaced by a placeholder text and NO image part is sent. By default the URL is the stored file URL (https or a presigned URL); with env LLM_VISION_IMAGE_USE_BASE64=1 LobeChat inlines a base64 data URI (contextBuilders/openai.ts L131-L145). The data URI below is the inlined variant.

cases.notes: Image input (docs/images.md): the data-URL image is decoded, checked and stored as an input file of the caller, and reaches an image-capable agent (the lab fixture agent declares image input) in its provider's own image shape. A text-only agent answers 400 unsupported_content with error.param on this part instead.

cases.title: 'Use Client Request Mode' on: the browser itself calls the gateway (openai-node in browser, no user field)

evidence.note: ModelRuntime created in the browser with dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true; same chatViaChatCompletions code path (options.user is undefined -> no 'user'); headers from openai-node browser build: X-Stainless-OS 'Unknown', Arch 'unknown', Runtime 'browser:<chrome|firefox|safari|edge|ie>', Runtime-Version '<major>.<minor>.<patch>' (detect-platform.ts L95-L105), no Node User-Agent override. Whether the browser also transmits a User-Agent header (set by the SDK, browser-dependent) was not verified.

cases.notes: Browser-direct: the response needs Access-Control-Allow-Origin (the preflight case below). Requires the user to be signed in to LobeChat for this mode to run at all.

cases.title: CORS preflight for the browser-direct (Client Request Mode) chat request

evidence.note: Non-safelisted request headers set by openai-node in a browser: authorization, content-type, x-stainless-arch, x-stainless-lang, x-stainless-os, x-stainless-package-version, x-stainless-retry-count, x-stainless-runtime, x-stainless-runtime-version (Accept is safelisted). openai-node also assigns 'User-Agent' and, when a per-request timeout is set, 'X-Stainless-Timeout'; whether a given browser lists 'user-agent' (and x-stainless-timeout) in Access-Control-Request-Headers was not verified, so a robust gateway should allow those two as well.

cases.notes: Only relevant when 'Use Client Request Mode' is on. Also applies to GET /v1/models if the browser performs model fetching itself (not verified). 204 is the more common preflight status; 200 listed per the test-lab convention.
